contributions.statement: When an LLM agent drives an acceptance or end-to-end test step by step, make it pick each next action from an enumerated list of currently valid actions referenced by id, with schema-checked JSON output and retry on invalid output; removing these constraints cut end-to-end success from 95.9% to 89.6% and lengthened runs (16.4 vs 15.1 actions, 5.7 vs 4.8 min).
contributions.evidence: §5.5 Table 5: 5 runs x 1,013 flows (5,065 executions per arm) on a frozen app build. Caveats: GPT-4o only, Uber mobile apps only, no run-to-run spread reported, and it is unclear whether the code-level schema validation of §4.3 was removed along with the prompt constraints.
relative_to: structured outputs / closed action space for tool-using agents

contributions.statement: Before giving an agent a large structured observation (a UI view hierarchy here; for a backend team, a schema or service graph), deterministically filter it to the elements the agent can act on; feeding the raw hierarchy instead lowered success from 95.9% to 91.7% and raised time per run from 4.8 to 5.6 minutes.
contributions.evidence: §3.4 Fig. 3 (144 nodes reduced to 51 executable actions) and §5.5 Table 5 (5,065 executions per arm, frozen build). Caveats: single model, single company, mobile UI rather than backend artifacts, no variance reported.

contributions.statement: When an agent-run acceptance test needs backend state that the UI cannot set reliably (for example an approval step), expose named, pre-stored API templates the agent may invoke instead of letting it compose raw calls; 23.1% of 1,013 production flows could not be authored without such calls.
contributions.evidence: §3.5-3.6 and §5.5 (234 of 1,013 flows need at least one in-flow backend tool call). Not ablated or compared with any alternative; the injection-prevention benefit of templates is asserted, not tested.

contributions.statement: Run agent-driven test flows daily against a curated set of golden trajectories, alert when action correctness falls below a threshold (95% here), and send only recurring, deduplicated divergences to weekly human triage; this kept reviewer effort to about 5% of time.
contributions.evidence: §4.2: about 10,000 validated trajectories, daily sampling, weekly triage. No comparison with any other monitoring scheme, no detection-rate data, and the 5% figure is self-reported.

reason: Only the Table 5 ablation is controlled. It yields two moderate, indirectly transferable refinements of known practice: an enumerated, schema-checked action space, and deterministic trimming of structured observations. The ROI, onboarding and pass-rate headlines are uncontrolled or estimated, and the template and monitoring designs are untested descriptions.
